periods.analysis: Case clearance closed 2024-Q3 at 57.2%, above the 55% target and in green status. With no prior quarter in this reporting run, I am treating 57.2% as the operating baseline for Harborview’s investigative follow-through. The result reflects steady work by the North Precinct case-screening desk, the Bayside property-crime pod, and the weekend detective rotation tied to the downtown waterfront routes. The important point is not just the number; it is that clearance is being achieved through documented case triage and timely victim contact, which protects community trust.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green result by keeping the 48-hour solvability review on all felony packets and selected high-harm misdemeanors. Extend the Bayside property-crime pod’s weekly evidence huddle to include digital-forensics intake from the Harborview Technology Unit. I want a simple audit trail on closed cases so the public can see disciplined process behind the 57.2% outcome.

periods.analysis: Case clearance improved to 59.2% in 2024-Q4, up 2.0 percentage points from 57.2%, and remained green. That movement is meaningful because Q4 typically brings holiday retail theft, package theft, and more calls around the Seaport Mall and ferry terminal corridors. Detectives used the November retail-theft emphasis list and coordinated with loss-prevention teams without letting lower-solvability cases clog the queue. The quarter shows that when patrol reports, evidence tagging, and detective assignment stay procedural, Harborview can raise clearance while staying consistent with due process.
periods.recommendations: Keep the Q4 retail-theft case packet template in place through the next holiday cycle and make it standard for commercial burglary reports citywide. Assign the Crime Analysis Unit to maintain a weekly repeat-location list for Seaport Mall, Harbor Landing, and the ferry garage. To sustain the gain from 57.2% to 59.2%, supervisors should review aged open cases over 30 days every Friday before shift close.

periods.analysis: Case clearance reached 60.1% in 2025-Q1, up 0.9 percentage points from 59.2%, keeping us green and above target for a third consecutive quarter. The first-quarter improvement came while the department was also absorbing new officer training blocks, so the investigative workflow held under competing demands. The East Harbor domestic-violence follow-up cohort and the Major Crimes evidence calendar helped reduce handoff delays after initial reports. I read this quarter as proof that a disciplined clearance process can mature without becoming mechanical or losing victim-centered contact.
periods.recommendations: Maintain the domestic-violence follow-up cohort and add a second weekly review slot for cases awaiting third-party records. Continue pairing newer officers with detective mentors for report quality checks, especially on assault, fraud, and vehicle-prowl cases. Because 60.1% is a strong position, the next action is to protect it with supervisor sampling of body-worn-camera references against written narratives.

periods.analysis: Case clearance was 59.5% in 2025-Q2, down 0.6 percentage points from 60.1%, but still green and comfortably above the 55% target. The slight decline is not unexpected as spring events, school-year incidents, and waterfront visitor traffic increase the number and variety of cases entering the system. Detectives reported more fraud and identity-theft packets tied to marina vendors and short-term rental activity, which often take longer because records sit with banks or platforms. The procedure is holding; the watch item is cycle time on cases dependent on outside records.
periods.recommendations: Sustain green performance by creating a 14-day tickler for bank, platform, and subpoena returns so fraud cases do not sit invisibly. Keep patrol report-quality coaching active during the spring event calendar, especially for cases generated around Pier 6, Old Harbor Park, and the marina lots. I also want the Crime Analysis Unit to separate fraud clearance timing from other property offenses in the next internal review.

periods.analysis: Case clearance moved to 58.2% in 2025-Q3, down 1.3 percentage points from 59.5%, while remaining green. This is the second consecutive decline, so I am not dismissing it even though the result remains above target. Summer tourism, beach-route disorder calls, and higher youth-related incident volume added pressure to detectives and community service officers alike. The procedural concern is not case quality overall; it is whether seasonal volume is stretching follow-up contact beyond the window when witnesses are easiest to reach.
periods.recommendations: Keep the summer beat detective schedule for the Waterfront, Dune Avenue, and Harbor High corridors through Labor Day plus two weeks, rather than ending it with the event calendar. Add a same-week witness contact requirement for solvable beach-route assaults, vehicle prowls, and thefts. To sustain green status, redeploy one light-duty officer to evidence-video retrieval from businesses participating in the Safe Harbor Camera Registry.

periods.analysis: Case clearance rebounded to 59.6% in 2025-Q4, up 1.4 percentage points from 58.2%, and stayed green. That recovery matters because it shows the summer decline was addressed through management action rather than explained away. The extended waterfront follow-up schedule, Safe Harbor Camera Registry pulls, and Friday aged-case reviews appear to have restored momentum before the holiday period. We are back near the earlier high-water mark while maintaining the procedural discipline that residents expect from this department.
periods.recommendations: Lock in the camera-registry retrieval protocol as a standing investigative step for commercial burglary, vehicle prowl, and assault cases. Continue Friday aged-case reviews, but add a monthly command-level look at cases open more than 60 days by unit and offense type. To extend the rebound from 58.2% to 59.6%, prepare the holiday retail-theft emphasis list by mid-October rather than waiting for Thanksgiving week.

periods.analysis: Case clearance reached 60.0% in 2026-Q1, up 0.4 percentage points from 59.6%, preserving green status and marking another quarter at or near 60%. This is a stable, credible result for a fast-growing coastal city where calls are rising alongside population and visitor activity. The detective bureau’s structured intake, the digital-evidence queue, and improved patrol narratives are now operating as a system rather than separate fixes. I am encouraged, but our message to the community should remain measured: clearance is strong because the process is being worked every day.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the 60.0% result by formalizing the detective intake checklist in the records management system before the next quarterly close. Expand report-writing feedback to all probationary officers and lateral hires assigned to the Central and North precincts. Use the Q1 training calendar to add a short module on victim re-contact standards so clearance gains do not come at the expense of communication.

periods.analysis: Case clearance ended 2026-Q2 at 59.1%, down 0.9 percentage points from 60.0%, but still green and above the 55% target. The dip follows a strong Q1 and coincides with the start of the summer event season, including Harborfest permitting, beach patrol deployment, and higher visitor-related theft volume. We have seen this seasonal pressure before, and the current result remains solid, but it reinforces the need to manage follow-up timing before Q3 volume peaks. The department is maintaining trust when it treats a green decline as a management signal, not a reason to relax.
periods.recommendations: Activate the summer clearance plan now: same-week witness contact, dedicated video retrieval, and a weekly aged-case review for Waterfront, Dune Avenue, and ferry-terminal incidents. Keep the 60-day open-case command review and add a Q3 dashboard cut for seasonal offenses so supervisors can see slippage early. To sustain green status from 59.1%, hold one detective back from nonessential event staffing each weekend to protect investigative follow-through.

periods.analysis: Clearance fell from 59.1% to 56.8% but remains above the 55% standard. Summer event demands and visitor-related cases continue to put pressure on investigative follow-up; the decline warrants attention despite the on-target result.
periods.recommendations: Protect detective follow-up time and review aged Waterfront and ferry-terminal cases weekly before the next reporting cycle.
